newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mixed.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mixed.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Monday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing
prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover was heavy at 2.087 billion yuan, though lower than 2.539 billion yuan last Friday.
The 30-day contract was the most actively traded.
Traders said trading volume had begun to pick up since last Friday when Beijing announced the establishment of a central state debt depository.
The set-up of the China Government Securities Depository Trust and Clearing Co will boost trading on the interbank market, traders said.

This is partly because non-banking financial institutions including securities houses will no longer be able to borrow funds from different T-bill repurchase markets around the nation using the same state debt certificates, they said.
"Institutions are expected to borrow more money from other markets and the interbank market will be a good choice," one trader said.
Traders said that securities houses were the most active traders on the interbank market today mainly due to the strong performance of the domestic A share markets.
They said they expected the rates to move steadily around the current levels in the absence of major negative news.
